gen-dafont-cheri-inter: Cheri has a calligraphic hand but no hairlines at all, every stroke as sturdy as a stem. Inter arrives with smooth, tube-like lines, and the pull between pen charm and clean build is the appeal.
gen-dafont-cheri-mulish: Cheri is a cute calligraphic hand with no hairlines whatsoever. Cheri's tall lowercase makes words look sturdy and large, while Mulish, a sans with open apertures and short ascenders, does the quiet work of being read.
gen-dafont-cheri-rubik: Sweet and sturdy: Cheri has a calligraphic hand, yet no swell on any downstroke, with tall lowercase. Cheri brings the charm; Rubik, with open round letters, handles the clear reading.
gen-dafont-college-fs-gambetta: Dynamic and tall, College draws every curve as stout as its stems. Gambetta, a serif, takes the page down to a moderate lowercase height, with wide-channelled counters and a graceful, gentle weight shift.
gen-dafont-college-lora: Blunt, tall and authoritative, College has virtually no stroke contrast. College earns its keep big and brief, while Lora thins its curves only slightly, like a candle flame, keeping a broad, welcoming c.
gen-dafont-college-noto-serif: College leaves the single-width trail of a rolling-ball pen, with big counters in tall lowercase. Noto Serif handles the literary reading with its subtle thick-thin cadence, leaving College to be dynamic and authoritative.
gen-dafont-conthrax-fs-gambetta: Geometric to the core, Conthrax gives its horizontals the same strength as its verticals, with a wide-mouthed lowercase a. Gambetta, a serif, then reads with a gentle, graceful sway.
gen-dafont-conthrax-lora: Clean and geometric, Conthrax draws a rope-thin outline with no thick or thin parts, its tall lowercase hugging the capitals. Lora then rolls on with a gentle thick-thin rhythm and a welcoming c.
gen-dafont-conthrax-noto-serif: Universal text meets geometric display: Conthrax holds its line width through every turn, with a wide-mouthed a. Noto Serif brings a tempered thick-thin variation that never hits razor-fine hairlines, so the two sit comfortably together.
gen-dafont-disorder-fs-gambetta: Disorder has no swelling where curves meet stems, and its glyphs sit well apart, looking raw and chaotic, with a high x-height. Gambetta settles things with bookish, graceful, gently thickening round letters.
